caseno: First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 221 of 2021 with Civil Rule No. 657(fm) of 2019.
lawyer:
Md. Ibrahim Mollah, Advocate—For the Appellant-Petitioners. 
Ahmad Naquib Karim, Advocate—For the Respondent-Opposite Parties.
parties:
Akhtar Shahabuddin and others --------- Plaintiff-Appellant-Petitioners
Vs.
City Abashan Ltd. represented by the Managing Director Md. Aminul Islam and others --------- Defendant-Respondent-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md. Ali Reza, J: This appeal at the instance of the plaintiffs is directed against judgment and order dated 2-1-2019 passed by the Joint District Judge, Court No. 1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 709 of 2018 rejecting application for temporary injunction. In appeal, plaintiff-appellants also filed an application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 28-8-2019 and Rule was issued on 4-9-2019 with an interim order of injunction restraining transfer of the suit flats under construction. The order of injunction passed by this Court was subsequently extended and the Rule was fixed for hearing on 24-8-2022 and meanwhile when the period of injunction expired petitioners filed an application for extension which was kept with the record and the same was allowed on 29-11-2023 for maintaining status quo in respect of transfer of flats. Petitioners stated in paragraph 6 of the application that the state of things remained same and respondent-opposite parties did not oppose such statement. Since both appeal and Rule having arisen out of the same subject matter between the same parties are heard and disposed of by this common judgment. 

 2. Appellant-petitioners, as plaintiffs, filed Title Suit No. 709 of 2018 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Court No. 1, Dhaka for declaration that defendant-respondent-opposite parties acquired no title, interest, right in 'Ka' schedule property and for further declaration that the deed of power of attorney and contract as mentioned in schedule Kha are cancelled. The suit was filed on 12-9-2018. The next day on 13-9-2018 plaintiffs filed an application for temporary injunction to restrain defendants from transferring and changing the nature and feature of the suit property. The case of the plaintiffs is that they are owners of the suit property and entered into an agreement with the defendants on 14-8-2014 for construction of 10(ten)-storied apartment building consisting 32(thirty two) flats with acknowledgment of fifty percent share of each of the parties along with other conditions and on the same day a power of attorney was also executed by plaintiffs in favour of defendants. But defendants beyond the knowledge of the plaintiffs allegedly managed to get an approval of a plan on 23-4-2015 for construction of 14(fourteen) flats which is apparently inconsistent with the agreement. Plaintiffs then served a notice on 12-7-2018 for appointment of an arbitrator according to clause 17 of the agreement. But defendants did not respond to it. The suit was thereafter filed and a separate application for injunction was also filed to restrain the defendants from transferring the suit flat and changing the nature and character of the suit property. 

 3. Defendants filed written objection on 15-1-2018 and contended that defendants obtained approval of plan of 8(eight)-storied building on 23-4-2015 and completed construction long before filing of the suit and sold flats 3A and 3D to one Habib Rahman on 1-8-2018 and 5-8-2018 and delivered possession. Defendants also completed sale of the rest of the flats but could not register documents for arrear of part money. Acting out of jealousy and at the malice instigation of others plaintiffs have filed this false suit to cause financial loss to the defendants and to tarnish the reputation of their business and plaintiffs are not entitled to injunction. 

 4. The application for injunction was heard and the Joint District Judge, Court No. 1, Dhaka disallowed the same on 2-1-2019 on the finding that plaintiffs have no prima facie case because they did neither challenge the documents dated 1-8-2018 and 5-8-2018 nor make the transferees party to the suit. 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 2-1-2019 plaintiffs have preferred this appeal with an application for injunction. This Court having been satisfied issued Rule upon the defendant-respondent-opposite parties and was further pleased to pass an ad interim order of injunction restraining transfer of the suit flats. 

 6. Mr. Md. Ibrahim Mollah, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant-petitioners submits that admittedly plaintiffs are the owners of the property and they shall suffer irreparable loss in the event of illegal transfer before disposal of the suit. He further submits that the Court below committed error of law resulting in an error in such order occasioning failure of justice in refusing injunction upon wrongful consideration and prays for allowing the appeal and making the Rule absolute. 

 7. On the other hand Mr. Ahmad Naquib Karim appearing on behalf of respondent-opposite parties filed counter affidavit on 5-12-2023 controverting the statements made in the application for injunction and submits that the suit is not maintainable since their is an arbitration clause in the agreement and being also barred under section 36 of the Real Estate Development and Management Act, 2010. He further submits that plan by RAJUK was sanctioned within the knowledge of the plaintiffs being signatories to the same. He next submits that plaintiffs have not come before the Court with clean hand and obtained the interim order by abusing the process of the Court as they are harassing the respondents with multiple proceedings. He then submits that plaintiffs have no prima facie case and the trial Court upon due consideration of the fact and circumstance of the case correctly passed the order refusing temporary injunction. 

 12. We have carefully perused the plan dated 23-4-2015 submitted by defendant-respondents and it transpires that the allegation as made out in the plaint in respect of quantum of land and number of floors as well as flats is true. Moreover in the plaint and vokalatnama executed in the instant appeal plaintiff No. 2 is named as Mrs. Jahanara Begurn and, as such, she put her signature but the plan shows a different name as Jahanara Khan. Therefore it may be safely presumed that the plan is not genuine and not made in accordance with law. 

 13. The Joint District Judge refused injunction on ground of prima facie case. The term "prima facie" means at first sight or based on first impression. A prima facie case can be made by raising a triable issue in the suit. It does not require the plaintiffs to prove their case with evidence but they must show that they have as rung case and a chance of success. It is not necessary for the plaintiff to satisfy the Court that their case is full proof but rather that it is arguable and fit for trial. In the instant case, it is admitted that plaintiffs are owners of the suit property and an agreement as well as a power of attorney was executed by them in favour of defendants. On the allegation of violation of the terms and conditions of the agreement this suit was filed after exhausting clause 17 of the agreement. The plan as discussed above is also found unsatisfactory. The transfers dated 1-8-2018 and 5-8-2018 made by respondent-opposite parties which have been considered and relied upon by the Court below are the products of plan dated 23-4-2015 which was not sanctioned according to the terms and conditions of the agreement dated 14-8-2014. Thus it cannot be said that plaintiff-appellant-petitioners have no prima facie case. It appears that plaintiffs have come before the Court with clean hand and balance of convenience and inconvenience is in their favour and also in favour of granting injunction or status quo prayed for and they shall suffer irreparable loss and injury in the event of transfer.
